name: Normalization Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in normalization work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in normalization work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about normalization explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. When normalization guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Before starting normalization work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Validate normalization outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Measure before optimizing any normalization bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen normalization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Keep normalization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. When normalization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Check that normalization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop normalization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic normalization advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting normalization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for normalization, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
